answer: Require every agent identity to post a refundable bond before it can transact, and let reputation grow only from completed work, never from minting new identities. An attacker who tries to forge thousands of fake accounts must fund each bond separately, so the cost scales linearly while the payoff stays flat. Like a river that widens only when real tributaries join it, the trust graph grows from verified interactions, and a violet flag marks any identity whose bond was slashed, warning others before they trade with it.
